He previously played for the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). ==Early life and career== Johnson was born in [[Fresno, California]]. He grew up around [[Phoenix Suns]] guard [[Jalen Green]] and considered Green to be like a big brother.{{Cite web |last=Insight |first=Pro |date=July 4, 2022 |title=AJ Johnson Q&A |url=https://www.prospectiveinsight.com/post/aj-johnson |access-date=June 24, 2024 |website=Pro Insight |language=en}} Sometime in 2020, during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Johnson had a growth spurt where he grew from 5 ft 10 to 6 ft 5.{{Cite web |date=November 21, 2022 |title=Texas adds No. 25 prospect Johnson to class |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35075799/texas-adds-no-25-prospect-aj-johnson-recruiting-class |access-date=June 24, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ==High school career== Johnson started his high school career at [[San Joaquin Memorial High School|San Joaquin Memorial]] in [[Fresno, California]] before spending two years at [[Taft High School (Los Angeles, CA)|Taft High School]] where he emerged as one of the biggest risers in part of a growth spurt in the 2023 class being one of the best combo-guards. Johnson for his senior year decided to attend [[Donda Academy]], [[Kanye West]]'s school in [[Simi Valley, California]].{{Cite web |last=Karamanos |first=Alex |date=August 11, 2022 |title=BREAKING: 2023 4-Star AJ Johnson will transfer to Donda Academy (CA) |url=https://www.circuitscouting.com/news_article/show/1235505-breaking-2023-4-star-aj-johnson-will-transfer-to-donda-academy-ca- |access-date=June 24, 2024 |website=Circuit Scouting |language=en-us}} After Donda Academy closed, Johnson finished his senior year at Southern California Academy.{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2022 |title=Donda players find programs; No. 8 recruit to OTE |url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/34941295/top-basketball-recruits-find-schools-donda-academy-closure |access-date=June 24, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} Johnson signed with Bill Duffy and WME Basketball. ===Recruiting=== Johnson was seen as one of the best guards and combo guards in the 2023 class. At one point, Johnson was ranked as the 9th or 10th best player in the class by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPN]], [[247Sports]], and [[On3.com|On3]]. On November 21, 2022, Johnson committed to the [[University of Texas]] choosing [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] over [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] and several other high-profile offers such as the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] and [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{Cite web |last=Conway |first=Tyler |title=5-Star Guard Prospect AJ Johnson Commits to Texas over Louisville, LSU, USC, More |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10056387-5-star-guard-prospect-aj-johnson-commits-to-texas-over-louisville-lsu-usc-more |access-date=June 24, 2024 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}} On April 13, 2023, Johnson announced his decommitment from Texas and announced his plan to sign with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League in Australia]], joining [[LaMelo Ball]], who went from a 2nd round pick to potential 1st pick with NBL's Next Stars program, as the second player to join the team out of high school.{{Cite web |date=April 13, 2023 |title=Projected '24 lotto pick opts for NBL over Horns |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/36178252/aj-johnson-decommits-texas-join-australia-nbl |access-date=June 24, 2024 April 13, 2023, Johnson signed a contract with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League in Australia]], joining the NBL's Next Stars program. Johnson joined [[LaMelo Ball]] in 2019 as the other American-born prospect to join the Hawks. Johnson averaged 2.9 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.7 assists per game in 7.7 minutes per contest playing 26 games during his time with the Hawks.{{Cite web |title=AJ Johnson International Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/aj-johnson-1.html |access-date=June 24, 2024 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2024–2025)=== On June 26, 2024, Johnson was drafted with the 23rd overall pick by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Select AJ Johnson With 23rd Pick In 2024 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-select-aj-johnson-with-23rd-pick-in-2024-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=June 27, 2024}} It was called a "surprising pick" and a reach by an older Bucks team as Johnson was expected to be selected somewhere in the second round, and was seen as a project despite late first round interest by teams.{{cite web|title=Bucks' AJ Johnson: Surprising pick at No. 23 to Bucks|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-aj-johnson-surprising-pick-at-no-23-to-bucks/|website=CBSSports.com|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}} On July 5, he signed with the Bucks.{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign AJ Johnson and Tyler Smith|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-aj-johnson-and-tyler-smith|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2024|access-date=July 5, 2024}} Johnson made his NBA debut on October 23, 2024, in a 124–109 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks at Philadelphia 76ers Box Score, October 23, 2024|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410230PHI.html|website=BasketballRef|access-date=November 1, 2024}} and throughout his rookie season, he has been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite web|title=2024–2025 Wisconsin Herd Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Wisconsin-Herd/50/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 18, 2024}} ===Washington Wizards (2025–2026)=== On February 6, 2025, Johnson was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in a four-team trade, alongside [[Khris Middleton]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-acquire-middleton-johnson-from-milwaukee-bucks|title=Wizards Acquire Middleton, Johnson From Milwaukee Bucks|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025}} On March 17, Johnson made his first career start in a 112–97 loss to the [[2024–25 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]], contributing eight points, seven rebounds, four assists, and one block.{{cite web | last1=Taylor | first1=Cody | title=How did AJ Johnson perform in his first career start? Wizards vs. Trail Blazers box score | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=March 18, 2025 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/did-aj-johnson-perform-first-180355311.html | access-date=December 2, 2025}} He made 22 appearances (including 11 starts) for Washington down the stretch, recording averages of 9.1 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 3.1 assists.{{Cite web|title=AJ Johnson 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5170947/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=April 14, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Johnson appeared in 25 contests for the Wizards in the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 2.8 points, 1.2 rebounds, and 0.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=AJ Johnson 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5170947/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=April 14, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2026)=== On February 5, 2026, Johnson, along with [[Marvin Bagley III]], [[Tyus Jones]], and [[Khris Middleton]] were traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[Anthony Davis]], [[Jaden Hardy]], [[D'Angelo Russell]], and [[Dante Exum]], in a three team trade that sent [[Malaki Branham]] to the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. As part of the trade, the Wizards also shipped off two first-round and three second-round picks to help facilitate the deal.{{Cite web |title=Anthony Davis traded to Wizards in 9-player, 3-team deal|url=https://www.nba.com/news/wizards-mavericks-anthony-davis-trade |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US }}{{Cite web |title=Anthony Davis traded to Wizards in
